title: Research: T185 dirty-entry and frame-refit screens on the #2863/#2894 words (negative result, no κ)
body:
## Summary

**Negative result. No κ claim. The selected record is unchanged.**

This package bounds the most direct native-word lever left after #2863 proved the fixed-inventory packing optimum: letting more helpers enter dirty **while every existing gate stays fixed**. The words screened are:

- the PR2857 shared-kernel words of #2863;
- the newer preload-move words of #2894 (Jeremy Kothe, 07:49 UTC).

| Word | Result |
|---|---|
| PR2857 base/extra | **0** of 184 eligible helpers have a frame-feasible dirty entry, in both `direct` and `pre-only` modes |
| PR2894 base/extra | **0** of 182 |
| One-hop relays, all four words | 8 apparent relays (409, 411, 413, 415, 425, 427, 429, 431), **0 valid** under an exact bilinear test |
| Frame refits (side check), all four words | 0 improving: single-gate moves (345 candidates) and forward/backward cascades (2797/3009 on PR2857, 2803/3015 on PR2894) |

- **Calibration.** On the older PR2833 words the same screen returns exactly #2853's 16 quartet helpers: {460,461,468,469}, {462,463,470,471}, {478,479,490,491}, {480,481,492,493}.
- **Frames are the obstruction.** With every frame constraint removed, all 184 eligible helpers of the PR2857 words are algebraically cancellable (`evidence/RELAXED-CENSUS.json`).
- **Consistency with #2894.** Its two new quartets, (456,457,466,467) and (458,459,464,465), all have a zero-frame first gate in the PR2857 words. That puts them outside the fixed-gate class screened here, and #2894 reaches them by re-synthesising the preload. The verifier asserts both facts.
- **Independent check of #2894's numbers.** This package's ledger reproduces its local profile {1:2404, 2:642, 3:262, 4:128, 5:26, 8:8} and inventory {8:86, 9:232}.

## Method

`tools/wordlib.py` is an independent, exact implementation:

- the PR2833/PR2857 frame-climb ledger;
- an adjoint pass giving every register's target-dirt response just before every program item. It reproduces the stored compensation for 402 of 408 live helpers on all six words; the six exceptions are warp-tainted initial-correction sources.

`tools/entry_screen.py` asks whether a helper's whole dirt response lies in the exact span of responses reachable by inserted gates `r += u*q0`:

- insertion at any time up to the helper's purity horizon, in either phase;
- partner cancellation;
- entry at a sub-frame of the first frame;
- frame feasibility over the full program timeline, including A/B pins, warps, restore and end frames;
- optional one-hop relays.

`tools/refit_screens.py` covers fixed-word frame moves. The card lists that class as a scope-change trigger (#1995/#2013), so it is labelled a side check.

## Verification

All checks are standard-library only.

```sh
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/t185-dirty-entry-frame-screens --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/t185-dirty-entry-frame-screens
```

| Check | Outcome |
|---|---|
| `--check-only` metadata | PASS |
| Registered replay, Python 3.12.13 | `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=negative-result` (exit 0, 414 s) |
| `core` / `chains2857` / `chains2894`, Python 3.14 local | 94 / 218 / 213 s; timeouts 300 / 450 / 450 |
| `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'` | 133 tests OK (5 skipped) |
| `scripts/check_research_commit.py --ref c291ad5` | PASS (24 files) |

The `core` part includes these controls:

- a corrupted compensation coefficient is detected;
- a broken frame chain is rejected;
- a de-optimised word (one climb split) is repaired by the refit screen;
- the frame-relaxed subset is entirely in span;
- the relay-validity test accepts six known relays of quartet helper 478.

`make verify` and the selected `frontier1094` replay were not run. This package changes neither the selected construction nor any existing artifact, and CONTRIBUTING asks for affected checks only.

During development, four screen bugs produced false positives before publication. Each was caught by building the word literally or by the control. They are listed in the README; the published tools implement the corrected rules.

## Independent reproduction of #2863

Recorded in `evidence/T185-REPLAY.json`.

- **Full cold replay:** PASS (exit 0, 1507 s; CPython 3.13.16, NumPy 2.5.4, SciPy 1.18.1, SymPy 1.14.0, mpmath 1.4.1). κ = 0.001720100805416885927944 − 10⁻⁴⁶ − 10⁻⁷⁰ exactly.
  - The release receipt differs from the published one only in a wall-clock `seconds` field and the manifest hashes derived from it. Substituting the published native hashes and `seconds` reproduces the published receipt exactly.
- **Fast replay:** all five stages pass.
  - The published head omits two `.gitattributes` files (`* -text`) that its MANIFEST lists, so `--hash-only` fails as published. Restoring them from #2857 matches the pinned hash.
  - Under Python 3.14 the regenerated `FILL.json.gz` differs only in its gzip container; the decompressed payload is identical.

## Scope, limits and overlap

- **Not covered:** changed gate schedules or preload/mixing blocks (the class #2894 uses), simultaneous multi-helper plans, relays longer than one hop, and operator-word corrections for warp-tainted helpers. A finite screen is not an impossibility theorem.
- **Overlap.** This complements #2875 (same account), whose screens covered adjoining one outside column and 94 entry/frame tests. It also overlaps lanes in the advisory structural investigation in Discussion #2612; no priority is claimed.
- **Open next questions** are in `TASK.json` and the README:
  1. re-route the remaining 84 zero-frame-first helpers' preload;
  2. joint multi-helper plans, e.g. 479 via 502/503/490;
  3. warp-tainted helpers.
- **Branch base.** The branch is built directly on the fork's main (`189b527`, an ancestor of upstream main). The package was verified on upstream main `47e4094`, and its tree object is identical in both commits. Only the 24 new package files change.

- **Packing optimum and dual prices:** Dugongue (#2863).
- **Retained lineage:** all contributors credited in those notices.
